subject: Bounded named-object admission for current-source publisher construction
claim: The read-only current-object admission stage accepts all six maintained native publisher objects, discovers moved startup entries, and rejects the selected malformed objects. The focused Windows owner passes. The same Windows-built test and structure-tool WVBs, packaged for Linux, execute successfully on real Debian. This is an object admission checkpoint, not a completed current-source transactional publisher.

source.value: Task changes over b02afa16, identified by source digests below. The existing package migration and Project 4 launcher working tree was preserved and is not promoted by this record.

runs.target: Current native publisher-object admission and structure-tool command
runs.command: pwsh -NoProfile -File Tools/Verify/Verify-Changed.ps1 -ChangedPath Linker/Windvale/Native-Current-Publisher-Object-Admission.wv -SkipDocumentationVerification. PlanOnly was reviewed first: one owner, expected 180 seconds, maximum 480 seconds. Final run returned 0, Tests: 1, Passed: 1, Failed: 0. Native self-test returned 42; CLI success returned 0 and wrong-role rejection returned 2.

runs.host: Windows x64 construction; Debian WSL native execution
runs.tool: Package-Hosted-Wvb.cmd profile 7, target linux; retained Current-Objects.elf and Current-Structure.elf
runs.command: Package each recorded WVB for Linux with a 120000ms construction deadline. On Debian, run Current-Objects.elf with the six maintained Linker/Reference/Consumers WVOs under timeout 90s; observed exit 42 and the six-role/moved-entry/oversized success report. Run Current-Structure.elf --current-object 6 with the shared transaction object: exit 0 and entry-offset=0 secondary-offset=3. The same object with role 5 returns 2.

limitations: No complete current-source publisher was linked or installed. Module/producer identity binding, dynamic segmented-image attachment, checked resolved relocation values, and transactional publication tests remain unfinished.
Object admission establishes structure and named ABI membership, not machine-code authenticity or behavioral correctness. No frozen artifact, pin, or serialized release request was changed.
The existing general WVO reader is reused under smaller preflight bounds. This checkpoint does not requalify the general reader or all native linker behavior.

The complete 16-case frozen publisher owner, broad changed-file selection, package conformance, installed toolchain checks, and cold cross-host qualification were not run. The focused selector extends the existing owner rather than adding a coordinator.

The final Windows run reused exact current-compiler and native product caches. Earlier development attempts exposed a duplicate local name, the old compiler's rejection, an incorrect SHA read-only alignment assumption, and Windows findstr exact-line handling of LF diagnostics; none was counted as passing evidence.

Linux products were cross-built from the recorded Windows WVBs. Debian execution is not independent source reconstruction. A read-only lookup found the current Debian compiler cache key absent; no cold reconstruction was started inside the focused check.
